How I Work

Research-first, opinionated about details, allergic to unnecessary meetings.

I start every project by trying to talk to five actual users before opening Figma — it's saved me from building the wrong thing more times than I can count. From there I move fast: rough wireframes, quick internal critique, a clickable prototype within a week.

I care a lot about the small stuff — empty states, error messages, the difference between a 200ms and a 400ms transition — because that's what makes software feel considered instead of just functional.

1. First

    Watch someone use it

    Before any drawing. Half an hour watching the actual job being done answers questions a workshop never gets to.

  2. Then

    The ugly version

    Rough, in front of people, early. Ideas are cheaper to throw away before they look finished.

  3. Then

    Make it boring

    Familiar patterns, predictable behaviour. In B2B software the interesting interface is usually the wrong one.

  4. Last

    Stay for the build

    Most decisions get made after handover. I would rather be there when they are.
